proposal.profile: AI engineer who takes LLM agents from prototype to deployment: for my AstraZeneca-affiliated MSc dissertation I deployed a tool-calling agent on AWS Lambda and checked it with a three-tier framework of ~65 automated tests. Deploys on AWS and GCP (Lambda, Cloud Run) with CI/CD and MLflow experiment tracking. At 180 Degrees Consulting, led the architecture in a five-person team that turned a startup client's loose brief into a working agent prototype within a three-month engagement, demoed it live (5-star rating from senior leadership), then contributed to the client's production MCP server, now in live use. Builds the modelling a brief needs and reports its limits plainly: gradient boosting (XGBoost churn), LSTM time-series forecasting with time-ordered validation, text clustering (SBERT, K-Means, DBSCAN) and 11,459 per-gene models (train Pearson 0.807 vs test 0.545).

needs_result.text: Integrated the agent into a React front end with real-time gene alias enrichment.
Reviewed pull requests in the client's production repository alongside the client's CTO, the engagement's point of contact.

Proposed the request flow: a user's text goes through the API and a customised prompt to the MCP server, where one LLM instance writes GraphQL queries against the client's Convex database and a second instance runs the statistical analysis before the result returns to the user.

Designed reproducible scikit-learn pipelines with feature engineering (temporal features, interaction terms, target encoding), model selection, cross-validation and hyperparameter tuning across classification and regression tasks.

Working independently for India-based startups and individual clients, built agentic RAG workflows (LangChain, LangGraph, ChromaDB) on GCP Cloud Run, NLP pipelines (Hugging Face Transformers, Ollama) and scikit-learn pipelines, served ML models as REST APIs (FastAPI, Docker), and contributed to a team LoRA fine-tune of a Llama model.

Needed a voice assistant that answers in real time and can be interrupted: built it end to end as a full-stack application (React front end, FastAPI and Google ADK back end, full-duplex WebSocket) with ReAct-based agent orchestration, barge-in handling and self-hosted speech models on Docker/CUDA (float16 inference, model warm-up) to cut latency.

bullets.text: Needed an agent that researchers could trust on a cancer research platform, including when its tools fail: built a tool-calling agent (LangChain, Claude Haiku 4.5 on AWS Bedrock) for three use cases (gene alias resolution, prompt-engineered explanations of a fixed scoring pipeline, validated dataset descriptions), with deterministic Ensembl and HGNC calls, deterministic hallucination guards, and circuit breakers with a 19,213-gene parquet fallback for when the external APIs are unavailable.

Built the Python data pipeline: reconciled 14 heterogeneous source datasets through identifier crosswalks so the agent used trusted data, then deployed it as a Docker image on AWS Lambda (ECR, least-privilege IAM) and documented the architecture and evaluation.

Working independently for India-based startups and individual clients, built agentic RAG workflows (LangChain, LangGraph, ChromaDB) on GCP Cloud Run, NLP pipelines (Hugging Face Transformers, Ollama) and scikit-learn pipelines, served ML models as REST APIs (FastAPI, Docker), and contributed to a team LoRA fine-tune of a Llama model.

Built a tool-calling LLM agent (LangChain, AWS Bedrock, Claude Haiku 4.5) for a multi-omics cancer research platform, with three tools for gene alias resolution, scoring-methodology explanation and dataset provenance.
Proposed and prototyped an MCP-based agentic tool in Python (FastMCP, Ollama gpt-oss:20b, PostgreSQL, GitHub Actions CI), presented in a live stakeholder demo.
Built scikit-learn pipelines and LSTM/BiRNN/CNN models in TensorFlow/Keras, deployed as FastAPI services in Docker.
Built a production RAG and agentic retrieval system (Claude API, LangChain, LangGraph, ChromaDB) served through a FastAPI REST API in Docker on GCP Cloud Run.
Deployed the agent as a Docker container on AWS Lambda (Lambda Web Adapter) with ECR image pipelines, IAM execution roles and least-privilege policies.

Wrote a three-tier test framework (tool-level, API/integration, live agent) of ~65 tests across 8 files, validated across the LLM provider migration from Groq to AWS Bedrock after a rate-limit evaluation.

A product-startup client needed an agentic AI prototype turned into software their team could use: led the architecture for a five-person cross-functional team, designed hierarchical agent workflows (MCP, Exograph GraphQL, PostgreSQL for persistent storage and retrieval across agent sessions) and built the Python prototype (FastMCP, Ollama, GitHub Actions CI), then ran a live demo with client stakeholders (5-star rating from senior leadership) within the three-month engagement.

paragraphs: Northwind Health AI needs the AI Engineer to deliver the work described in this ad. That is the kind of problem I have been working on. For my AstraZeneca-affiliated MSc dissertation I built a tool-calling LLM agent that keeps working when its data sources fail, deployed it on AWS Lambda and checked it with a three-tier framework of ~65 automated tests. After a rate-limit evaluation moved the agent from Groq to AWS Bedrock, I used the same tests to confirm it still behaved.

I care about the parts that make AI usable: grounding answers in trusted data through deterministic lookups, hallucination guards, and fallbacks for when external APIs go down. I also wrote the project's agent evaluation, including a documented hallucination-rate analysis. At 180 Degrees Consulting I prototyped an agentic tool for a loosely defined client brief and contributed to the client's production MCP server, now in live use; senior leadership rated the engagement five stars. At the Bristol × UWE AI Hackathon I paired a deterministic matching engine with a single LLM call, answering in under 3 seconds at about £0.003 per query. As a freelance engineer I built a production RAG and agentic retrieval system with LangChain and LangGraph.
Your ad asks for the work this role would own, which is the work I want to do next.
Could we spend 20 minutes on what the first problem in this role would be?
